nodes.speaker: ops
nodes.text: Day 84! The rotation lander glows on the horizon, bringing the new crew.

variants.text: Day 84! The rotation lander touches down on our sunlit ridge pad, bringing the new crew.
Day 84! The rotation lander creeps past the crater edge, bringing the new crew.

nodes.fact: NASA's Artemis plans have astronauts staying on the Moon for longer and longer trips, starting with about a week.

nodes.speaker: arch
nodes.text: Ines Duarte walks the new crew through the base: the dust airlock, the water recycler and the quirky pump.

variants.text: Ines Duarte walks the new crew through the base, including the seals that once leaked and the lesson about leak tests.
Ines Duarte walks the new crew through the base, and points out the lander that landed a little crooked.

nodes.fact: Real crews write lessons-learned notes after missions so the next team doesn't repeat the same mistakes.

nodes.speaker: sci
nodes.text: Dr. Okafor has months of data on ice, dust and radiation to hand to the next team.

variants.text: Thanks to the extra science rack, Dr. Okafor has a record-breaking pile of data for the next team.

nodes.fact: Apollo astronauts brought back 382 kg of Moon rocks. Scientists are still studying them today.

nodes.speaker: psy
nodes.text: Time to go home. How do you say goodbye to the new crew?
nodes.fact: Apollo 11 left a plaque on the Moon that reads: We came in peace for all mankind.
